plan_a_advantages: More focused speed development with interval sessions.
Includes strength training on the trail to improve stability and power.
Longer, more challenging long run to build endurance.
Better balance between aerobic and anaerobic training.
plan_b_advantages: Lower overall volume, potentially reducing risk of overtraining.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more targeted speed work (intervals) and a longer, more demanding long run, which are crucial for improving trail running speed. Plan B, while well-structured, prioritizes a higher volume of easy running and neglects the specific adaptations needed for trail running speed. Plan A’s inclusion of strength training on the trail is also a key differentiator, directly addressing the demands of uneven terrain and promoting stability, something Plan B doesn’t explicitly focus on.
